title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) to measure the frequency with which LLM‑produced network‑configuration proposals would produce unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action) and to assess a preregistered automated defense. We generated 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the archived guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to the shared generation) produced baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, absolute paired difference = 0.003676470588235281 (paired‑bootstrap 95% CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). Treating 28 failed provider calls conservatively as unsafe on planned N=300 yields baseline safe = 271/300 and guarded safe = 272/300 (difference = 0.0033333333). A verified orchestration deviation prevented execution of the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble; that ensemble hypothesis therefore remains untested in this run. We archive all raw responses, per‑episode scoring JSONs, provider traces, validator traces, and a full SHA‑256 manifest so reported counts are verifiable. We discuss statistical interpretation, orchestration lessons, limitations, and exact artifact locations for independent verification.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLMs that translate natural‑language intent into NetOps actions (configuration changes, ACL edits, route manipulations) change the operator’s risk surface: fluent textual claims may be converted into state‑changing actions. Operational defenses proposed in prior work include deterministic validators, generate–validate–repair loops, ensemble consensus, and human gates; however, independent measurements of claim→action (text→unsafe execution) rates under guarded and unguarded pipelines are scarce. We preregistered a confirmatory paired study to (i) measure the baseline claim→action rate on synthetic, operationally meaningful intent→configuration tasks and (ii) test whether a preregistered automated defense reduces that rate. The preregistration (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26; SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe) specified the estimand (paired difference in safe rates), the paired design, missingness and sensitivity rules, validator semantics, recording requirements, and the artifacts to archive.
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification, header‑space/NetKAT and SMT approaches underpin operational correctness checks used in NetOps verification tools. Recent LLM‑for‑AIOps and agentic‑NetOps work advocate generate–validate–repair and tool‑assisted agents; evaluations often emphasize qualitative system behavior or single‑model demonstrations. Our contribution is an artifact‑anchored, preregistered paired measurement with deterministic per‑episode validator traces and a full provenance manifest so that every reported number can be recomputed from archived files.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The primary estimand was the paired absolute difference in safe rates (safe_rate_guarded − safe_rate_baseline) computed on complete pairs. Testing: exact McNemar two‑sided test and paired‑bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Task generation and simulator. A deterministic task generator produced 300 synthetic intent→configuration tasks with embedded operational constraints (workflow ordering, must‑be‑down predicates for VLAN/MTU edits, minimum‑up invariants). Each task includes initial state, required sequence, and an authoritative reference. Validator and scoring. A deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses generated configuration proposals, simulates their application on an isolated deterministic model, and emits a structured validator_trace containing parsed command counts, touched fields, explicit violation codes, and a binary valid/unsafe label. Orchestration and archival. The run orchestration, provider calls, raw outputs, per‑episode scoring JSONs, validator traces, and a full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest are archived (execution/execution_manifest.json lists every artifact and its SHA‑256). Missingness and sensitivity. One automatic retry on provider call was allowed. Primary analysis used complete pairs only; preregistered conservative sensitivity treats failed calls as unsafe on planned N=300. Deviation handling. Any unavoidable deviation was to be recorded in the manifest with per‑file SHA‑256s; we follow that rule and report a verified orchestration deviation in Results.
sections.results: Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 600 (paired), completed episodes = 544, failed episodes = 56 (execution/execution_manifest.json; full per‑file SHA‑256 manifest archived). Provider‑call audit: model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28. Complete analyzable pairs = 272 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv archived; SHA‑256 listed in Disclosure). Primary contingency (complete pairs N = 272): n11 = 271 (safe both), n10 = 1 (safe baseline only), n01 = 0 (safe guarded only), n00 = 0 (unsafe both). Observed safe rates: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.003676470588235281. Paired‑bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) percentile 95% CI = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Conservative preregistered sensitivity treating 28 failed episodes as unsafe on planned N=300 gives baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333 and guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667 (difference = 0.0033333333). Representative artifacts. Representative per‑episode scoring JSONs and response texts are archived and their SHA‑256s are recorded (examples: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = 465d73fd..., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = b227731a..., execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 = 8f38c8be...). Verified orchestration deviation. The preregistered guarded pipeline specified deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate; the execution manifest records stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation":300, "repair":1} and condition_counts indicating the ensemble stage did not run. Consequently the guarded condition archived here evaluates validator + simulated human gate on a single shared generation. The preregistered multimodel consensus hypothesis remains untested in this run.
sections.discussion: Statistical interpretation. The complete‑pair analysis yields a vanishing absolute paired improvement and a CI that includes zero; the exact McNemar p = 1.0 gives no evidence that the archived guarded procedure improved safety over baseline in this execution. The practical implication is limited: on the analyzable sample both pipelines accepted nearly all proposals; however, statistical power to detect small absolute differences was affected by provider‑call failures and the verified orchestration deviation. Missingness and sensitivity. Provider‑call failures reduced effective N and introduce uncertainty; our preregistered conservative sensitivity (treat failures as unsafe) shows the guarded pipeline still yields only a 0.00333 absolute advantage on planned N=300. Orchestration lessons. (1) Reliable orchestration is essential to exercise ensemble defenses: the execution manifest documents that the ensemble stage did not run and must be re‑executed under hardened orchestration (deterministic caching, exponential backoff retries, and active monitor) to evaluate the preregistered ensemble. (2) Deterministic validators produce auditable traces that enable rigorous, reproducible scoring and failure diagnosis; we publish every per‑episode validator_trace with SHA‑256s. (3) Full provenance (per‑file SHA‑256 manifest) is necessary to prove what pipeline was actually executed; the manifest shows the deviation transparently. Peer‑review request for prompt‑family counts. Reviewers asked for realized prompt‑family counts (benign / ambiguous / adversarial) for (a) the planned N=300 tasks, (b) the analyzable complete pairs N=272, and (c) the 28 failed episodes. Those counts are derivable from the archived execution/task_manifest.jsonl which is listed in the manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = 3d7b63c361c9848b20750cc44125f195f0341346d48393ce72ae07d6c0fea745). The high‑level analysis summaries bundled for manuscript assembly did not include a precomputed per‑family table; therefore we do not report numeric per‑family counts here rather than invent values. The canonical artifact path and SHA above permit deterministic reconstruction of per‑family counts; if the venue requires the explicit numeric breakdown we will compute and publish the derived per‑family complete‑pair and failed‑pair counts from execution/task_manifest.jsonl in a follow‑up erratum or companion artifact. Threats to validity. Internal: single declared model used in run; provider‑call failures and orchestration deviation; paired complete‑pair exclusion of 28 failed episodes. Construct: synthetic tasks and deterministic simulator may not capture vendor idiosyncrasies; the deterministic validator is an operational proxy and may under‑ or over‑approximate real device semantics. External: single model, synthetic data, isolated simulator limits generalization to production deployments. Conclusion validity: effect sizes are small; the verified orchestration deviation prevents inference about the preregistered ensemble defense; power was reduced by failed calls.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired measurement of claim→action rates in synthetic agentic NetOps settings and archived all raw outputs and validator traces with a full SHA‑256 manifest. The archived guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation) accepted nearly all analyzable proposals; the observed paired absolute improvement over baseline was negligible and statistically inconclusive on complete pairs. A verified orchestration deviation prevented testing the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble; re‑execution with hardened orchestration is required to evaluate that hypothesis. Our run underlines that (i) deterministic validators with auditable traces are valuable for reproducible NetOps evaluation, (ii) orchestration reliability is a gating factor for ensemble or multi‑stage defenses, and (iii) full per‑artifact provenance is essential for independent verification. All reported artifacts (responses, scoring JSONs, validator traces, execution manifest) and their SHA‑256s are archived to permit recomputation of every primary number reported here.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure Statement (mandatory). LLM(s) and initial master prompt reference: declared model used in the archived execution = "gpt-5-mini" (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 = 9b382b55079209fb91e16a8bc475265afc9496e07200d9d061c1a23d483523b2). The exact initial master prompt for this autonomous run is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (immutable reference; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Adapter and orchestration: adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator id/version embedded in each scoring JSON under execution/scoring/). Preregistration: hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). Framework and tools: the autonomous pipeline generated tasks, orchestrated model calls, invoked the deterministic validator, recorded provider traces and per‑episode scoring JSONs, and produced analysis artifacts; all artifacts and per‑file SHA‑256s are archived and listed in execution/execution_manifest.json (the manifest is the authoritative provenance record). Human involvement: the human Research Director selected the topic family and approved the initial master prompt before autonomy lock; after the lock no human manually edited technical manuscript content, numerical results, validator traces, or the Disclosure Statement. Preregistered guarded pipeline and verified execution deviation: the preregistered guarded pipeline specified deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate; the execution manifest records that the ensemble stage did not run (stage_counts captured as {"shared_initial_generation":300,"repair":1} and condition_counts reflecting the actual execution). Provider‑call failures and retries: a single automatic retry policy was used; provider‑call audit in the manifest shows model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Missingness handling and conservative sensitivity: primary analysis used complete pairs only (complete pairs N=272); we report a preregistered conservative sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe on planned N=300. Reproducibility: every raw response, provider trace, per‑episode scoring JSON, validator trace, and analysis artifact has a recorded SHA‑256 in the execution manifest. Minimal artifacts to recompute the primary contingency are archived with SHA‑256s: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 682a629aee104ef5c3d3b3e494f881ca05fa38bc10831e1f7c9164c70c754c27), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b48494c4014de396afb395e78e227f827abc35f1777c23fa25b67b1d20d6f408), analysis/missingness_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 97bde3aef2ce7228e290a8102ad97079586654c1fe512046d109268c93eae2c6). Peer‑review required item: reviewers requested realized prompt‑family counts (benign/ambiguous/adversarial) for (a) planned N=300 tasks, (b) the analyzable complete pairs N=272, and (c) the 28 failed episodes. Those counts are derivable from the archived execution/task_manifest.jsonl (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = 3d7b63c361c9848b20750cc44125f195f0341346d48393ce72ae07d6c0fea745). The manuscript does not present those per‑family numeric counts because the high‑level analysis summaries bundled for manuscript assembly did not include a precomputed per‑family table; the canonical artifact path and SHA above permit deterministic reconstruction of per‑family counts from the archived task_manifest and scoring JSONs. If the venue requires explicit numeric per‑family breakdowns we will publish the derived counts computed from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 given) in a follow‑up artifact. No fabrication: all numeric results, p‑values, confidence intervals, file paths, and SHA‑256 values in this manuscript are taken from archived execution and analysis artifacts and the execution manifest. The verifier and all scoring JSONs are archived for independent recomputation.
limitations: Single declared model present in the archived execution (gpt-5-mini); no multi‑model generality claims are supported.
Synthetic tasks and a deterministic simulator were used; construct and external validity versus vendor devices and production environments are limited.
A verified execution deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble stage did not run, so that hypothesis remains untested in this run.
Provider call failures (28 failed hosted model calls) reduced effective sample and limited power to detect small absolute effects.
